newsitem.title: UK: Summary of latest opinion polls on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Summary of latest opinion polls on EMU.

text.p: The following is a summary of the findings from recent opinion polls concerning European economic and monetary union (EMU).

FINLAND, Feb 17 - Four of five members of the Finnish parliament declined to state their opinion on whether Finland should join EMU, a pro-EU lobby said. All 200 MPs were asked to respond in writing to questions relating to EMU. Of the minority who gave their opinion on Finnish membership of EMU, 66 percent were largely in favour although many attached conditions to their support.

PORTUGAL, Feb 13 - Most of Portugal's top politicians, civil servants and business people favour a referendum on the Maastricht Treaty, according to a poll by the Superior Institute of Corporate and Labour Studies. The poll said 76 percent of the country's elite backed a referendum, with 21 percent opposing.

SWEDEN, Feb 12 - A poll published by Swedbank showed 81 percent of the 40 New York, London and Frankfurt analysts surveyed believed the probability of Sweden taking part in EMU from the start was less than 50 percent.
FRANCE, Feb 5 - A SOFRES survey for Pelerin Magazine found that 55 percent of French people would vote "no" to the Maastricht Treaty and 45 percent would vote in favour.
GERMANY, Jan 31 - A survey of financial experts by the Handelsblatt newspaper showed optimism for a timely start to EMU rose to 79 percent in January from 76 percent in December.

BRITAIN, Jan 27 - An ICM poll for the BBC's Panorama programme showed that while 54 percent of those questioned were opposed to a single currency, 65 percent felt they were poorly informed. Sixty-one percent said they did not understand the meaning of "convergence criteria".

EUROPE, Jan 22 - A poll of forecasts conducted by Consensus Economics Inc showed Germany, France, the Netherlands and Belgium were unanimous choices as core members of EMU. More than 70 percent of forecasters also expected Austria, Ireland and Finland to be founder members.
FRANCE, Jan 21 - A CSA/Humanite Dimanche poll showed 67 percent of French people would support a referendum on a single currency, and if consulted, 61 percent would support the euro.
FINLAND, Jan 14 - More than 70 percent of Finnish industrial firms think Finland should be in the first EMU wave, a survey by the Confederation of Finnish Industry and Employers (TT) showed.
DENMARK, Jan 13 - A majority of Danes want a referendum on currency union, according to a Greens poll. Over 19 percent are opposed and 19.4 percent do not know, the poll showed.
FRANCE, Jan 13 - An Ipsos opinion poll showed that 56 percent of French people would vote for the introduction of a single currency if a referendum were organised.
EUROPE, Jan 10 - A poll for Britain's Daily Telegraph, France's Le Figaro, Germany's Handelsblatt and the Italian news magazine L'Espresso showed support for a referendum on the euro.

Asked if they favoured a referendum, the "yes" replies were British 76 percent, German 79 percent, French 66 percent and Italian 52 percent. Support for a single currency would be 71 percent in Italy and 61 percent in France; some 44 percent of Germans and 56 percent of British citizens would vote no.
The poll was conducted by Gallup in Britain, Gallup-Germany, Groupe IFOP in France and DOXA in Italy.

GERMANY, Jan 9 - A poll by the FORSA opinion research institute found that 56 percent of Germans opposed and 31 percent supported an EMU start in 1999. Seventy-three percent demanded a national vote on the country's entry to EMU.
FINLAND, Jan 8 - Research institute Taloustutkimus Oy found 45 percent of Finns opposed EMU while 36 percent supported Finnish participation.
GERMANY, Jan 3 - Germany will not meet the fiscal criteria for EMU membership, according to a survey of economists by magazine Boerse Online.
BRITAIN, Jan 2 - The 1996 UPS Europe Business Monitor, an annual survey of business leaders, showed Britain was the most euro-sceptic country in the EU.

EUROPE, Jan 1 - KPMG Management Consulting found in a Europe-wide survey that while 93 percent of respondents believed their country would eventually enter EMU, two thirds had no plans in place to cope with it.

FRANCE, Jan 1 - An Ifop survey showed 79 percent of French citizens saw the drive towards a single currency continuing in 1997. Sixty-two percent said they hoped it would continue versus 35 percent against.
GERMANY, Dec 31 - A poll by the INRA institute found 53 percent of Germans surveyed felt the euro would bring them disadvantages while only 30 percent saw benefits.
